preconditions.description: The input string S has length at most 40 characters.
The input string S contains only alphabetic characters, '@', '.', '+', '-', '(', ')', ' ', or digits.

preconditions.expression: S.count('@') == 1 and S.count('.') >= 1 or all(c.isdigit() or c in {'+', '-', '(', ')', ' '} for c in S)
preconditions.description: The input string S is either a valid email (contains exactly one '@' and at least one '.') or a valid phone number (contains only digits and allowed formatting characters).

preconditions.expression: len(S) >= 8 if '@' in S else len(S) >= 10
preconditions.description: If S is an email, its length is at least 8; if S is a phone number, its length is at least 10.

postconditions.expression: @ in S and (return_value == S.lower() and all(c == '*' for c in return_value[1:-1] if c.isalpha() and c != return_value[0] and c != return_value[-1]))
postconditions.description: If S is an email, the output is the lowercase version of S with all letters between the first and last letter of the first name replaced by exactly 5 asterisks ('*').

postconditions.expression: @ not in S and (return_value == '+' + '***-***-***-' + S[-4:] if '+' in S or any(c in {'+', '-', '(', ')'} for c in S) else '***-***-' + S[-4:])
postconditions.description: If S is a phone number, the output exposes only the last 4 digits and masks all other digits. The country code (if present) is masked as '+***-***-***-', and the local number is formatted as '***-***-1111'. Extraneous formatting characters are removed.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == (len(S) if '@' in S else (4 + 3 * 3 if '+' in S or any(c in {'+', '-', '(', ')'} for c in S) else 4 + 3 * 2))
postconditions.description: The output length matches the expected masked format: for emails, it preserves the original length; for phone numbers, it follows the masked pattern length (e.g., 12 characters for '+***-***-***-1111').
